content: 1. Dextrose reduces magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 2. Calcium carbonate increases the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction is serious and requires the use of alternative therapies. The interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 3. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of diltiazem through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring is recommended. 4. Magnesium hydroxide decreases dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after medications containing polyvalent cations. Use alternative therapy if available. 5. Calcium carbonate decreases dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after polyvalent cation-containing medications. 6. Doxercalciferol increases magnesium hydroxide levels by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 7. Magnesium hydroxide decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Separate administration by 2 hours. 8. Calcium carbonate decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Separate administration by 2 hours. 9. Drospirenone increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. Drospirenone decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 10. Calcium carbonate decreases eltrombopag levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. 11. Separate administration from antacids by at least 2 hours. 13. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of enalapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 14. Calcium carbonate increases ephedrine levels by passive renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Calcium carbonate interacts with erdafitinib. Avoid co-administration during the initial dosing adjustment period (first 21 days). Serum phosphate binders may obscure decisions regarding dosage increases. 16.
